security_audit.summary: The audit confirmed the real risk is concentrated in recalc.py, which runs LibreOffice and writes a persistent macro into the user LibreOffice profile. The hardcoded URL and SKILL.md backtick detections are false positives caused by XML namespaces and Markdown formatting, but the profile modification and external command execution require remediation.

remediation.issue: Persistent LibreOffice macro is written to the user profile.
remediation.suggestion: Use an isolated temporary LibreOffice user profile for recalculation, or require explicit user consent and remove the macro after use.

remediation.issue: LibreOffice is launched against user-supplied workbook paths.
remediation.suggestion: Validate input paths and extensions, keep shell execution disabled, enforce timeouts, and clearly disclose that files may be modified in place.

remediation.issue: Filesystem writes are not scoped to the workspace.
remediation.suggestion: Limit generated files to a project or temporary directory and document every write that affects application configuration.

finding_verdicts.reason: The script launches LibreOffice headlessly to initialize the user profile before adding a macro. The command uses fixed arguments, but it still performs external process execution with side effects outside the workbook.
This subprocess call only probes whether gtimeout is installed using fixed arguments. It does not include user-controlled command construction and does not perform sensitive work.

The script runs LibreOffice against a user-supplied workbook path and invokes the installed macro to recalculate and save the file. There is no shell injection vector, but the external command can modify files and process untrusted documents.
The string is an XML namespace inside LibreOffice macro metadata, not an outbound network request. No network client or data transfer is present at this location.
The code targets the hidden LibreOffice configuration directory under the user home directory. This is a persistent application-profile location, not a project-scoped workspace file.
The script reads and later writes files under the hidden LibreOffice profile. This is a real hidden-file access pattern with lasting user-environment impact.
The code writes Module1.xba into the LibreOffice macro directory. The macro content appears intended for recalculation, but writing an application macro is still a sensitive filesystem action.
The script creates the LibreOffice macro directory in the user profile if it does not exist. This is a real filesystem side effect outside the skill workspace.

content.value_statement: Spreadsheet work often fails when formulas, formatting, and source data are handled separately. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through reliable workbook creation, editing, analysis, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Reads Excel, CSV, and TSV data with pandas workflows.
Creates new XLSX workbooks with formulas, sheets, formatting, and widths.
Edits existing workbooks while preserving formulas and workbook structure.
Applies financial model conventions for colors, number formats, and assumptions.
Uses a LibreOffice helper script to recalculate formulas and report formula errors.
Documents common openpyxl and pandas safeguards for large or formula-heavy files.
limitations: Formula recalculation depends on LibreOffice being installed and callable as soffice.
The helper script can modify the workbook and the local LibreOffice user profile.
Very large workbooks may be slow because the validation scan checks every cell.
The guidance does not replace manual review for complex Excel compatibility issues.

use_cases.title: Analyze a Data Workbook
use_cases.description: Inspect sheets, summarize columns, identify missing values, and produce a clean workbook-ready summary.

use_cases.title: Build a Financial Model
use_cases.description: Create formulas, assumptions, formatting, and validation checks for a structured finance workbook.

use_cases.title: Maintain Operational Templates
use_cases.description: Update existing workbooks while preserving established formulas, styles, and sheet conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Workbook Contents
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an existing file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the workbook named workbook.xlsx. Summarize each sheet, key columns, row counts, missing values, and any visible data quality concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Formatted Tracker
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a simple workbook from user requirements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an XLSX tracker for monthly sales by region. Include input columns, total formulas, clear headers, number formats, and a summary sheet.

prompt_templates.title: Update an Existing Template
prompt_templates.scenario: Modify a workbook without breaking its structure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the existing workbook template.xlsx with the new dataset. Preserve its formatting, formulas, sheet names, and current layout conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Formula Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workbook creation with recalculation checks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a three-year financial model with assumptions, linked formulas, formatting, and source notes. Recalculate formulas, fix every formula error, and report the validation result.

output_examples.input: Create a revenue forecast workbook with assumptions and totals.
output_examples.output: A workbook with assumptions, monthly revenue calculations, summary totals, formatted headers, and validation notes showing no formula errors.

output_examples.input: Review this workbook for formula problems.
output_examples.output: A concise audit that lists affected sheets, error types, cell locations, likely causes, and recommended fixes.

output_examples.input: Update the customer export with cleaned columns and a pivot-ready sheet.
output_examples.output: A cleaned workbook with normalized column names, preserved source data, and a separate analysis-ready sheet.

best_practices: Keep assumptions in separate cells and reference them from formulas.
Preserve existing template styles unless the user requests a new format.
Recalculate and verify formula-heavy workbooks before delivery.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding calculated results that should remain dynamic formulas.
Saving a workbook opened with data_only mode when formulas must be preserved.
Changing established template formatting without checking existing conventions.

faq.question: What file types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It focuses on XLSX workbooks and also describes workflows for CSV, TSV, XLSM, and related spreadsheet data.

faq.question: Can it create formulas?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides formula creation and recommends using workbook formulas instead of hardcoded calculated values.

faq.question: Does it recalculate formulas automatically?
faq.answer: It provides a LibreOffice-based helper script for recalculation when LibreOffice is installed.

faq.question: Can it preserve existing workbook formatting?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions emphasize studying and matching existing workbook styles before making edits.

faq.question: Is the recalculation helper risk free?
faq.answer: No. It runs LibreOffice and writes a macro into the local LibreOffice profile, so users should review that behavior first.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
